behavior_constraints: docs/analysis_rules.md must state that for duplicate (epoch, step) shard entries with different metric values, the earliest timestamp wins.
Timeline conflict resolution must retain the earliest-timestamp entry among conflicting same (epoch, step) shard entries instead of the latest.
Existing timeline command output structure must remain unchanged; only merged metric values may differ.
A `mlforge diff <evidence-dir> <file1> <file2>` subcommand must be added and documented in docs/spec.md and docs/output_schema.md.
On success, diff must write JSON to stdout with status `ok`, `file_a` and `file_b` as basenames of the two inputs, and a `tensor_diffs` array.
`tensor_diffs` must contain one entry per tensor name present in either checkpoint, sorted lexicographically by tensor name.
`shape_a` or `shape_b` must be null when the tensor is absent from that file; `shape_match` must be true only when the tensor exists in both files and shapes are identical.
`max_abs_diff` and `mean_abs_diff` must be present only when `shape_match` is true and must be computed over float32 element-wise absolute differences.
summary must include total_tensors_a, total_tensors_b, common_tensors, shape_mismatches, and lexicographically sorted only_in_a and only_in_b arrays.
If either checkpoint filename does not exist under the evidence directory, the command must exit non-zero and print an error to stderr.

behavior_constraints: NOT is a prefix operator with highest precedence, so `NOT epoch == 0` excludes all epoch-0 entries.
AND binds tighter than OR.
Parentheses override default precedence; `(step < 5 OR step > 95) AND epoch == 0` must group the OR first then apply AND.
`loss > 1.0 OR NOT grad_norm > 5.0 AND epoch == 3` parses as `loss > 1.0 OR ((NOT (grad_norm > 5.0)) AND epoch == 3)`.
Malformed parenthesized queries such as `(step < 5` or `step < 5)` must exit non-zero with an error message on stderr.
The grammar must follow: query := or_expr; or_expr := and_expr ("OR" and_expr)*; and_expr := not_expr ("AND" not_expr)*; not_expr := "NOT" not_expr | atom; atom := "(" or_expr ")" | condition.
Supported fields remain step, epoch, loss, lr, grad_norm, acc, event, ts.
Comparison operators remain >, <, >=, <=, ==, !=.
All existing query syntax must continue to work after the changes.
